brief.headline: Continuity Guardian could not produce a grounded review
brief.what_broke: 12 session(s) waiting on locks. Root blocker(s): pid 112047 (batch_worker/batch_replayable_inventory, idle in transaction, txn open 4.0s) blocks 1 session(s); last statement: SELECT 1
brief.who_is_affected: Checkout success 27% over 30s (88/120 failed) vs SLO 95%. Revenue run-rate $18,400/min; about $13,493/min at risk. Verification window 10s. The business tolerates at most 60s of degraded checkout.

options.description: Terminate the root blocker session (batch_worker/batch_replayable_inventory, pid 112047) to release its locks.
Take no action; let the blocker finish and monitor checkout recovery.
options.cost: about $13,493/min of checkout revenue at risk while waiting

brief.recommendation: pid 112047 (batch_worker/batch_replayable_inventory) is idle in transaction with txn open 4.0s and blocks 1 session; 12 sessions are waiting on locks [DB-1]. Checkout is at 53% success with 28 timeouts in 15s [TEL-1], and business impact shows 27% success over 30s with $13,493/min at risk vs SLO 95% [BIZ-4]. Waiting costs ~$201,500 and exceeds the 60s degradation tolerance [BIZ-5]. The workload is replayable (replay cost 4 min, policy may_interrupt) [BIZ-2], no protected settlements are in flight [DB-2], and no change-calendar window covers it [BIZ-3]. Memory confirms terminating batch_replayable_inventory previously restored checkout to 100% over 10s [MEM-1].

audit.report: A replayable inventory reconciliation batch worker (pid 112047) held an idle transaction open for 4.0 seconds and blocked checkout sessions, driving success from 53% over 15 seconds down to 27% over 30 seconds with 88 of 120 requests failing. The Database Guardian proposed terminating the batch worker because waiting would cost about $201,500 and exceed the business's 60-second degradation tolerance, while termination meant only a 4-minute replay of an idempotent, checkpointed job. The Continuity Guardian failed to produce a grounded review twice, so the negotiation escalated to inventory-platform without executing any action. Checkout remained degraded and the business was not recovered within the incident window.
audit.root_cause: The batch_replayable_inventory workload held an idle open transaction that blocked checkout sessions, and no guardian action was executed to release the block before the incident window closed.
lessons: For batch_replayable_inventory, pre-approve termination of idle-in-transaction replayable batch workers because the job is idempotent, checkpointed, replays in about 4 minutes, and waiting costs far more than the replay.
audit.negotiation_critique: The Database Guardian built a complete, evidence-backed case and did not waste its round, but the Continuity Guardian failed grounding twice and contributed no evidence, causing the only round to end in escalation without execution.
follow_ups: Ask inventory-platform to confirm why pid 112047 stayed idle in transaction for 4.0 seconds and to add an alert for long-running idle batch transactions.
Document the pre-approved termination path for batch_replayable_inventory in the runbook so the next negotiation can execute in round one.
